episodes.title: Why I Am a Protestant   Yet I Will Rejoice
episodes.description:
Catholic, Orthodox, or Protestant: what separates the three branches of Christianity, and why does it matter? In this episode, Brandon Anderson explains why he is unashamedly a Protestant. Starting with Martin Luther and the Reformation, he walks through the five solas: Scripture alone, grace alone, faith alone, Christ alone, and to the glory of God alone. Along the way he looks at why Scripture is the final authority over tradition and the Pope (2 Timothy 3–4), why no indulgence, pilgrimage, or work can earn salvation (Ephesians 2), how the thief on the cross was saved by faith without ever being baptized (Luke 23), and why Jesus' sacrifice on the cross was sufficient once for all. Brandon also shares why he believes there are true followers of Jesus in all three branches, and why these five truths still shape his life today.

episodes.title: Should Christians Trust AI With Their Questions?
episodes.description:
More people, especially teenagers, now take their hardest questions to AI before they ever ask a pastor. In this Ask Away! Live Q&A, Brandon Anderson and Joshua Garner talk about why that matters. AI can gather information and arrange it into knowledge, but wisdom begins with the fear of the Lord, and a machine can't fear God. We talk about AI's counterfeit humility, why it tends to tell us what we want to hear (2 Timothy 4), how the Holy Spirit gifts believers to serve one another (1 Peter 4), and why pastors can bear fruit in a way AI never can (Matthew 7). AI is a useful tool, and Christians have no reason to fear it, because Jesus is Lord over all of it.

18:06 Reading Scripture Honestly: Jesus and Noah

episodes.meta: The topic of whether or not drinking alcohol is sinful is often debated among Christians.
key_points: The Bible condemns drunkenness but not drinking alcohol itself.
Christians should obey the law, follow their conscience, avoid causing others to stumble, pray, know themselves and listen to others.
Don't pressure others to drink, don't let alcohol become an idol, and don't project your convictions on others.
Reading Scripture honestly means not importing abstinence into it. Jesus and Noah both appear in passages involving wine.
If you are convicted not to drink, don't. If you are not convicted and avoid drunkenness, you can drink in faith.

episodes.meta: From timeless line dances to popular social media dances, dancing is an enjoyable pastime that often brings people together.
key_points: The Bible never calls dancing a sin. David danced before the Lord in 2 Samuel 6, and Scripture speaks of dancing in celebration.
The episode gives four wisdom principles: follow your convictions, be mindful of others, seek the Lord in prayer and act in faith, and don't project your convictions on others.
Having a conviction against dancing is not wrong, but declaring it a sin when God has not said so is speaking for God.
Brandon enjoys dancing, especially at weddings, as a way to rejoice with God's people.

episodes.title: What is sin?
episodes.description:
Christians will often use the word sin, but what exactly does it mean? In today’s episode, Brandon gives a definition of sin and talks about how we can know what is or isn’t sinful. He also discusses how Christians should respond to their sin and attempt to become more righteous before a Holy God.

episodes.meta: Christians will often use the word sin, but what exactly does it mean?
key_points: Sin is anything we think, say or do that is contrary to the nature and character of God.
Sin separates us from God and the wages of sin is death, but Jesus died that death so that believers can be made right with God.
All have sinned, and good works cannot outweigh sin.
The Old Testament law divides into civil, ceremonial and moral law, which helps Christians discern what still applies.
Christians are no longer slaves to sin (Romans 6) and should flee sin and pursue righteousness.

episodes.title: What is the Great Commission?
episodes.description:
Christians talk often about the Great Commission! But what is it, and what are followers of Christ supposed to do about it? In this episode Brandon talks about what the Great Commission is, and what that means in the life of a Christian.

0:00 Introduction: What Is a Commission?
1:46 Matthew and the Great Commission
3:49 "Go and Make Disciples"

episodes.meta: Christians talk often about the Great Commission! But what is it, and what are followers of Christ supposed to do about it?
key_points: A commission is an assignment to complete a mission. The Great Commission in Matthew 28 is Jesus' command to his followers.
The commission is to go and make disciples and to teach them to observe all that Jesus commanded.
That includes a call to live righteously, which is impossible alone. Christians are freed from sin by Jesus and strengthened by the Holy Spirit.
Jesus sympathizes with our weaknesses and promises to be with us always.
Like Paul in Philippians 4, we can be content in every circumstance and do all things through Christ who strengthens us.

episodes.title: How should Christians view the death penalty?
episodes.description:
This topic is a controversial topic, but what does the Bible say about this, and how can we apply that to how we view this as Christians? In this episode Brandon will seek to answer that question from this listener submitted question.

0:00 Introduction
1:40 The Death Penalty Under the Old Testament Law
3:42 Jesus Fulfills the Ceremonial Law
7:49 Civil Law and the Nation of Israel
11:44 The Woman Caught in Adultery
15:49 Turning the Other Cheek
17:41 Government's Role in Justice
19:59 Grace, Unity and Where We Land
episodes.meta: This topic is a controversial topic, but what does the Bible say about this, and how can we apply that to how we view this as Christians?
key_points: The Old Testament law God gave Israel prescribed the death penalty for certain crimes, and the host holds that the law and its punishments were perfect and just.
Scholars often divide that law into ceremonial, civil and moral categories. Jesus fulfilled the ceremonial law, and Christians are not under Israel's civil law.
The New Testament gives no explicit instruction on the death penalty. In John 8 Jesus does not condemn it but shows grace, and in Matthew 5 he calls his followers to go beyond "an eye for an eye."
Government exists to bring justice on wrongdoers, protect against invasion and keep the peace. Brandon believes the death penalty can be just in some cases, while warning that it has been abused.
Christians can land in different places on this issue and should stay united in Christ rather than divide over it.

episodes.title: Why did Jesus have to die?
episodes.meta: Why did Jesus have to die? Sin deserves death, the penalty had to be paid, and Jesus took it on our behalf. A Bible-based answer from Brandon Anderson.
episodes.summary:
Jesus had to die because God is consistent, holy and just: sin is rebellion against Him, the penalty for sin is death, and that penalty has to be paid. Brandon explains the wages of sin (Romans 6:23), why Scripture ties forgiveness to the shedding of blood (Hebrews 9:22), and how Jesus, who lived without sin, took the punishment in our place so that believers receive His righteousness.

The resurrection proved that Jesus is who He claimed to be. Brandon closes with a story of two brothers to picture what substitution means.
key_points: God doesn't change, so His righteous judgment against sin is consistent (Hebrews 13:8).
Sin is anything we think, say or do that is contrary to God's nature, and its wages is death (Romans 6:23).
No amount of good deeds can cancel wrongdoing, just as past kindness doesn't erase a murder at trial.
Without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness (Hebrews 9:22); Jesus' sinless life made Him the suitable sacrifice.
God showed His love by sending Christ to die for us while we were still sinners (Romans 5:8, John 3:16).
The resurrection proves who Jesus is and shows He conquered both sin and death.
This gift is received by faith in Jesus (2 Corinthians 5:21).
episodes.description:
This is a question that many Christians have asked throughout the life of the Christian Church. So what does the Bible say in regards to this question? In this episode, Brandon will seek to answer that question based on what scripture says, and why it was necessary for Jesus to die.

key_points: Prayer is simply communicating with God and being in relationship with him, and God hears our prayers.
Jesus taught his disciples how to pray, and the Lord's Prayer is a good place to start.
The PRAY acronym is a helpful tool: Praise, Repent, Ask, Yield to God's will.
Practical help includes removing distractions, writing out your prayers and praying without ceasing.
Scripture is full of examples, such as Hannah and the church in Acts 4, of praying boldly in hard circumstances.

episodes.title: What does it mean to be created in the image of God?
episodes.description: The Bible tells us that all people are created in the image of God, but what exactly does that mean? Ultimately, the Bible doesn’t tell us, and that has led to several different opinions on the subject. In today’s episode, Brandon discusses the ways we aren’t like God, as well as how we reflect being made in the image of God, which include being relational, creative, and valuable.
episodes.meta: The Bible tells us that all people are created in the image of God, but what exactly does that mean?
key_points: Scripture clearly says all of humanity is created in God's image (Genesis 1:26), but it doesn't give an exact definition of what that means.
Common views include dominion, creativity, relationality and eternality, and the host suggests it is likely an element of all of them.
Being in God's image makes every human being valuable, regardless of size, wealth or background, from conception (Psalm 139).
It doesn't make us like God in every way: we are not all-powerful, everywhere present or all-knowing.
Because people matter, God made a way to restore us through Jesus, who is the perfect example of the image of God (Hebrews 1).

episodes.title: How do I read the Bible?
episodes.description:
All Christians have struggled with knowing how to study the Bible. Whether you’ve been a Christian for 10 minutes or 10 years, it’s difficult to understand where to start or how to stay motivated when reading the Scriptures. In today’s episode, Brandon outlines what’s most important to keep in mind when reading the Bible and gives some tips and tricks if you’re looking to better understand the Word of God.

0:00 Introduction: What Is the Bible?
1:37 Just Start: The Bereans
3:25 Context, Context, Context
7:13 Study Tools: Study Bibles and Commentaries
9:08 Choosing a Translation
12:39 Genre: Law, Poetry and Prophets
14:52 Example: Studying Philippians
19:19 Just Dive In, and Closing
episodes.meta: All Christians have struggled with knowing how to study the Bible. Whether you’ve been a Christian for 10 minutes or 10 years, it’s difficult to…
key_points: The Bible is a cohesive collection of writings by over 40 authors across about 1,500 years, written mainly in Hebrew and Greek, that tells God's plan of redemption.
Just start, as the Bereans did, and don't be intimidated by how much there is.
The three most important words in studying Scripture are context, context, context: a passage cannot mean something other than what it meant to its original audience.
Study Bibles, commentaries and a reliable translation are helpful tools.
Notice the genre, whether law, poetry or prophecy, and apply principles, as in the example of Philippians.

episodes.title: How can I know that I am a Christian?
episodes.description:
One of the biggest questions Christians ask themselves is how do I know if I am truly saved? Lies from Satan will tell us we aren’t children of God and lead us to question our faith in Jesus. In today’s episode, Brandon lists several reasons from Scripture why we shouldn’t believe the lies from the enemy and instead can have full assurance of salvation in Jesus Christ.

0:00 Introduction: Assurance of Salvation
0:24 What Is a Christian?
3:52 Adopted as God's Children
5:58 God's Discipline Shows His Love
11:23 Fruit: Evidence of a Changed Life
15:34 Unrepentant Sin and Holiness
18:54 Examine Yourself
21:02 God Is Faithful, and Closing
episodes.meta: One of the biggest questions Christians ask themselves is how do I know if I am truly saved?
key_points: A Christian is a biblical disciple of Jesus, someone who believes what Scripture says about who he is and trusts in him.
Anyone who believes in the Lord Jesus is saved and adopted into God's family as a child and joint heir with Christ.
God's discipline is evidence of his love for his children.
A changed life bears fruit: believers increasingly look like Jesus, and unrepentant sin is a warning sign to examine yourself.
Assurance rests on God's faithfulness: he keeps his promises.

episodes.title: Is it important for Christians to go to church?
episodes.description:
As Christians is it important for us to go to Church? In this episode, Brandon looks at the importance of being together as the body of Christ, both for the Church, but also for individual Christians.

0:00 Introduction: Defining Our Terms
0:42 The Church as Christ's Body and Bride
5:58 Don't Neglect Meeting Together
8:25 Living Life Together
10:17 The Answer: No Lone-Wolf Christians
13:38 Those Who Leave the Church
15:32 Church Hurt and Using Your Gifts
17:52 Conclusion
episodes.meta: As Christians is it important for us to go to Church? In this episode, Brandon looks at the importance of being together as the body of Christ, both…
key_points: Yes: the Bible leaves no room for lone-wolf Christians. The church is Christ's body and bride, and Jesus established and loves it.
Hebrews says not to neglect meeting together, and believers need each other for mourning, joy, accountability and encouragement.
The church is the universal body of believers, made up of the local churches we gather in.
Church hurt is real, but it doesn't justify cutting yourself off from the gifts and community God provides.
Every Christian has gifts to use in the local church for reaching the world with the gospel.

episodes.title: How should I respond to the election as a Christian?
episodes.description:
Politics have always been a difficult topic, and especially around election time tensions are high. However, as Christians, we are called to a higher standard even with politics.

This week Brandon discusses how we should respond to the election results regardless of who we voted for!

0:00 Introduction: The Election Is Over
1:34 Jesus Has All Authority
3:24 Romans 13: Government's God-Given Purpose
5:17 Render to Caesar: Submitting to Authority
9:14 Praying for Our Leaders
10:58 When to Obey God Rather Than Men
13:21 Conclusion
episodes.meta: Politics have always been a difficult topic, and especially around election time tensions are high.
key_points: How Christians respond to government doesn't depend on who holds office: Jesus has all authority.
Romans 13 teaches that government has a God-given purpose, and Jesus said to render to Caesar what is Caesar's, so Christians submit by obeying, respecting and praying for those in authority.
Pray for leaders, including those you didn't vote for.
When an authority commands what God forbids, we must obey God rather than men, as Peter and John did in Acts. Pray for wisdom to know when that applies.
The host hopes most Christians never face that conflict, and that Peter's "obey God" and "submit to the king" are held in balance.

episodes.title: Are Mormons and Jehovah's Witnesses Christians?
episodes.description:
The Bible teaches that there is only one God and that Jesus is God. This belief is at the heart of Christianity. Mormons have added to the biblical account and believe the revelation from Joseph Smith supersedes Scripture. Jehovah’s Witnesses believe in multiple gods and have changed Scripture to align with this claim. In today’s episode Brandon discusses these different beliefs and explains why Christians, Mormons, and Jehovah’s Witnesses are not the same.

0:00 Introduction: Defining "Christian"
0:32 Adding to the Biblical Account
1:14 Did Christians Corrupt the Bible?
4:58 Many Gods vs. One God
7:19 Jesus' Claim Before the High Priest
9:21 "You Are Gods": Psalm 82 and John 10
11:38 So, Are They Christians?
episodes.meta: The Bible teaches that there is only one God and that Jesus is God. This belief is at the heart of Christianity.
key_points: A Christian is a believer and disciple of the biblical Jesus, who is fully God and fully man, sinless, and the fulfillment of Old Testament prophecy.

The host's answer is no: Mormons and Jehovah's Witnesses who follow their churches' doctrine do not follow the biblical Jesus, because those teachings add to or change the biblical account of who he is.
The episode examines the claim that Christians corrupted the Bible, the idea of many gods versus one God, and Jesus' claim to be God before the high priest.
It looks at "you are gods" in Psalm 82 and John 10 and what Jesus meant there.
The host encourages Mormons and Jehovah's Witnesses to connect with a church that worships the biblical Jesus, and warns against false teachers (1 Timothy 6).

episodes.title: How do I share the Gospel?
episodes.description:

In today’s episode, Brandon discusses four of these common excuses, as well as several reasons why we shouldn’t let those excuses prevent us from sharing the Gospel. He also gives some practical tips that will help you go into the world and share the Gospel with others!

0:00 Introduction: What Is the Gospel?
1:36 You Don't Need to Know Everything
3:42 The Great Commission: We Are All Sent
5:37 Facing Opposition
7:39 Not Ashamed of the Gospel
9:22 Don't Be Afraid: God Is for Us
11:53 How to Share the Gospel
14:17 Pray for Boldness
18:08 A Story From Uganda
episodes.meta: Sharing the Gospel can be difficult, and Christians often have a list of excuses why they don’t think they can do it.
key_points: The gospel is the good news that God made a way for sinful humanity to be right with him through the death, burial and resurrection of Jesus, fully God and fully man.
You don't need to know everything to share it. The Great Commission sends every believer, and God goes with us.
Expect opposition, but don't be ashamed or afraid, since God is for us.
Pray for boldness, and then simply do it rather than making excuses.
A story from Uganda shows how one person sharing the gospel can lead to another sharing it with a friend.

episodes.title: What is the Gospel?
episodes.meta: What is the gospel? The good news that God did what we couldn't: Jesus lived, died and rose so we can be right with God by faith.
episodes.summary:
The gospel means "good news," and at its core it is this: God did what we couldn't. Brandon walks from creation and humanity's rebellion through the Old Testament promises of a Messiah to Jesus, who lived a sinless life, took the punishment for our sin on the cross and rose again.

Salvation is a gift received by faith, not something earned by good works (Ephesians 2:8), and it is good news meant to be shared with everyone.
key_points: "Gospel" simply means good news: what Jesus Christ has done to make a way for us to be right with God.
God created everything good. Humanity rebelled, and sin and death entered the world.
Even our best efforts can't repair the relationship (Isaiah 64:6), because God requires perfection.
The Old Testament promised a Messiah who would descend from Abraham, be a prophet like Moses, reign as David's king and bear our punishment (Isaiah 53).
Jesus, fully God and fully man, lived sinlessly, died in our place and rose again.
Salvation comes by grace through faith, as a free gift (Ephesians 2:8).
episodes.description:
The word “Gospel” is thrown around a lot today. But what does it really mean? How does Jesus and the Bible fit into the Gospel? Here Brandon answers the question of what is the Gospel, and why it matters to you!

0:00 Introduction: The Meaning of "Gospel"
0:44 Creation: God Made Everything Good
2:10 The Fall: Humanity Rebels
4:14 God's Promise of a Chosen One
6:17 A King From David's Line
8:45 Jesus Christ, the Messiah
11:09 The Cross and Resurrection
12:59 Telling the World, and Closing

episodes.title: What does it mean to be a Christian?
episodes.description: A Christian is not just someone who believes that Jesus was a historical figure, prophet, or good teacher. A Christian is a disciple of Jesus. In today’s episode, Brandon talks about where Christians first got their name, what it means to be a disciple of Jesus, and once you are a Christian, what your next steps should be.
episodes.meta: A Christian is not just someone who believes that Jesus was a historical figure, prophet, or good teacher. A Christian is a disciple of Jesus.
key_points: The word Christian first appeared in Acts 11:26 in Antioch, likely as a derogatory term that believers came to wear as a badge of honor.
A Christian is a disciple of the biblical Jesus. Believing he was merely a historical figure, prophet or good teacher isn't enough.
The biblical Jesus is fully God and fully man, the Christ, who died for our sins and rose bodily from the grave.
Being a Christian means following him, not just believing facts about him.
Next steps: get involved in a church and Bible study, and grow through Scripture and prayer in the process of sanctification.

episodes.title: Is Jesus God?
episodes.description: Not only does the Bible claim Jesus was the Messiah and a prophet, but it also says Jesus is God. In today’s episode, Brandon discusses how Jesus claimed to be God and what people today believe about Him. Is He a liar, is He a lunatic, or is He Lord?
episodes.meta: Not only does the Bible claim Jesus was the Messiah and a prophet, but it also says Jesus is God. In today’s episode, Brandon discusses how Jesus…
key_points: The Bible claims Jesus is the Messiah, the promised Christ (Mark 8:29), and a prophet greater than Moses (Acts 3:22).
Jesus claimed to be God: before the high priest in Matthew 26, who understood it as blasphemy, and when he quoted Scripture to Satan in Matthew 4.
Others claimed it too: John 1 says the Word was God and became flesh.
The resurrection is key: over 500 people saw the risen Jesus (1 Corinthians 15), and his followers, including Peter and Paul, gave up everything for that claim.
If Jesus rose, he is who he claimed to be: fully God and fully man.

episodes.title: If God is good, why do bad things happen?
episodes.meta: If God is good, why do bad things happen? Brandon answers from Scripture: a broken world, no one righteous on their own, and a patient God who sent Jesus.
episodes.summary:
Bad things happen because we live in a broken world, not because God is absent or unkind. Brandon opens with compassion for anyone going through something hard right now, then explains that God made the world good, that humanity's rebellion brought sin and death, and that Scripture says no one is righteous on their own (Romans 3).

He argues God's goodness shows in sending Jesus, in joining us in our brokenness, and in patiently delaying judgment so more people can come to know Him.
key_points: The brokenness we see in relationships, health and finances traces back to the fall, not to God's original design (Genesis 1–3).
Scripture says no one is righteous on their own (Romans 3:10–12, 23), which changes the question "why do bad things happen to good people?"
Even our good works are like filthy rags before a perfect God (Isaiah 64:6).
God's goodness shows in sending Jesus: the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life (Romans 6:23).
Jesus joined us in this broken world and sympathizes with our weakness (Hebrews 4:15, John 1:14).
God is also just and will one day destroy all evil; His patience in the meantime lets more people come to faith.
episodes.description:
Brandon answers one of the most-asked questions to Christians: Why does God allow bad things to happen to good people?

We've all wondered why good things happen to bad people. So why exactly does it happen? If God is so good, why does He let it happen?

Whether you've been a Christian for a long time or you barely know the name “Jesus” this question comes up in life almost daily. So let's dive in and find out how the Bible answers this tough question!

0:00 Introduction: Why Do Bad Things Happen?
0:40 We Live in a Broken World
1:58 The Fall: Genesis 3
4:00 No One Is Righteous
8:10 God's Rich Mercy and Grace
9:10 God Joined Us in Our Brokenness
11:11 Closing: Are You Seen as Righteous?

episodes.title: What is the Bible?
episodes.meta: What is the Bible? One story of redemption written by 40+ authors over 1,500 years. How it is organized, why Christians trust it, and where to start.
episodes.summary:
The Bible is a collection of writings by more than 40 authors across about 1,500 years, written in Hebrew, Greek and a little Aramaic, that tells one unified story of God's plan to redeem humanity. Brandon explains why Christians believe it is inspired and preserved by God (2 Timothy 3:16, 2 Peter 1:20–21) and traces that story from creation and the fall through the promises about the Messiah to Jesus and the gospel.

He also lays out how the Old and New Testaments are organized and suggests that new readers begin with the Gospel of Luke.
key_points: The Bible is not just one book: it was written by 40+ real people with real lives, over roughly 1,500 years, in three languages.
Christians believe Scripture was inspired by God and preserved by His Spirit (2 Timothy 3:16; 2 Peter 1:20–21).
Its unified story: God created everything good, humanity rebelled, and God made a way back through Jesus.
Old Testament genres: law, history, poetry, and the major and minor prophets. New Testament: the Gospels, Acts, Paul's letters, other letters and prophecy.
The Bible isn't arranged strictly in chronological order.
If you're new to reading it, start with the Gospels, perhaps Luke, which pairs with the book of Acts.
episodes.description:
Have you ever wondered what the Bible really is? Is it really just an old, dusty irrelevant book or is it much more than that? The Bible is an old book, yes, but is it still relevant? And if it is, how should that affect our lives?

We delve deeper into what the Bible truly is and strive to answer common questions about the most influential book in history!

0:00 Introduction: The Most Influential Book in History
0:32 One Book, Many Authors
3:41 Creation and the Fall
6:18 God's Promises: Abraham and David
8:49 Jesus Fulfills the Promises
12:52 How the Bible Is Organized
15:12 Where to Start Reading
15:59 Closing

episodes.title: Why the name "Yet I Will Rejoice"?
episodes.description: In the Old Testament, there was a prophet by the name of Habakkuk who harshly questioned God and asked why so many bad things were happening. We will discuss the conversation God had with Habakkuk and, ultimately, why we chose Habakkuk 3:18 as the inspiration for this podcast.
episodes.meta: In the Old Testament, there was a prophet by the name of Habakkuk who harshly questioned God and asked why so many bad things were happening. We will…
key_points: The podcast is named after Habakkuk 3:17-19: "Though the fig tree may not blossom... yet I will rejoice in the Lord."
Habakkuk was a prophet in dark times who strongly questioned what God was doing as empires fought and judgment loomed.
Nothing in his circumstances changed, but his perspective did, and he could rejoice in the God of his salvation.
The show's goal is for people to know God and rejoice in him regardless of life's questions and obstacles.

key_points: Sylvie, a high school student, tells how she started a Christian club at her school and led among her peers.
She wanted to reach students who hadn't heard about Jesus and equip others to be on fire for the same mission.
She encourages other students to just do it, find community and support, and not go it alone: "lone wolf Christianity is not a thing."
In hard moments she holds on to the fact that Jesus is with us in the trials, "the fourth man in the fire," and his word will not return void.

episodes.title: How do I deal with anxiety?
episodes.description:
Anxiety is a crippling problem faced by many in this day and age. So how do we deal with it when we see it in our peers and experience it ourselves? The root of anxiety is fear, but Scripture tells us to “not be afraid” 365 times! As Christians, we have no reason to be afraid and Brandon dives into how we can accomplish that in this next episode.

0:00 Introduction: Anxiety Is Rooted in Fear
2:02 Do Not Be Afraid, and the Fear of the Lord
6:35 Our Accountability Before God
9:04 Philippians 4: Rejoice Always
12:54 Focus on Who God Is, Not "What If"
15:15 Be Anxious for Nothing: Prayer and Peace
17:35 Don't Look at the Pothole
19:35 Think on What Is Lovely
22:10 Closing
episodes.meta: Anxiety is a crippling problem faced by many in this day and age. So how do we deal with it when we see it in our peers and experience it ourselves?…
key_points: Anxiety is rooted in fear of the unknown, and Christians have no reason to be afraid because of Jesus.
Be thankful for what God has done in salvation and in providing for you in your own life.
Philippians 4 says to rejoice always and be anxious for nothing, bringing everything to God in prayer so his peace guards your heart.
Focus on who God is, not on the "what ifs" or the circumstances. Dwelling on circumstances, such as through social media, feeds anxiety.
Think on what is true, lovely and praiseworthy; your circumstances may not change, but your outlook will.

episodes.title: How do I deal with church hurt?
episodes.description:
Church hurt is something many Christians and non-Christians have experienced in one form or another. While Christians are called to be above reproach and love like Jesus, the sinfulness of humanity often stands in the way.

This week Brandon discusses how we should respond when we experience church hurt, and how we can heal, as well as help others to heal from past experiences of church hurt, ultimately by trusting in Christ!

0:00 What Is Church Hurt?
1:55 Brandon's Story of Church Hurt
7:03 Lesson 1: Know God Through His Word
10:39 God Sees, and Vengeance Belongs to the Lord
13:00 God Fights Our Battles
16:45 Truth Always Produces Fruit
19:47 The Church Is the Bride of Christ
24:30 When It's Right to Leave a Church, and Recap
episodes.meta: Church hurt is something many Christians and non-Christians have experienced in one form or another. While Christians are called to be above reproach…
key_points: Church hurt is real: God uses sinners to build his kingdom, and sometimes people are seriously hurt in the church.
Know God through his Word, because he sees what is done in secret and vengeance belongs to the Lord.
God fights our battles, and truth always produces fruit.
The church is the bride of Christ, so don't throw the baby out with the bathwater or isolate yourself from the body.
Sometimes it is right to leave a particular church, but stay involved in the life of a local church rather than just sitting in a pew. Brandon shares his own story.

episodes.meta: September 10, 2025 was filled with great sadness, and many individuals around the world are mourning the events that took place. Today, we are wanting…
key_points: A special live episode recorded the day after Charlie Kirk was killed, and after a shooting at Evergreen High School in Colorado.
Philippians says to rejoice and be anxious for nothing, and Psalm 46 says there is no reason to fear, even amid frightening news.
Be careful with news and social media, and pray for boldness as the early church did in Acts.
Habakkuk wrestled with violence and injustice and ended with "yet I will rejoice," the show's namesake.
Mourn with those who mourn, pray for the Kirk family and the victims, and hold on to resurrection hope.

episodes.title: How should Christians respond to the current Trump presidency?
episodes.description:
A few months into the Trump Presidency and there are many opinions on how this Presidency is going. Whether or not you like, or even love what Trump is doing Scripture tells us how we are supposed to respond to our authority.

0:00 Introduction
1:42 Jesus Has All Authority
3:39 Romans 13: Government as God's Servant
5:33 Praying for Leaders and Not Trusting in Nations
9:29 Psalm 46: No Reason to Fear
11:31 Daniel: Standing for Truth Under Authority
13:27 Our Response, Whatever Our Opinion of the President
episodes.meta: A few months into the Trump Presidency and there are many opinions on how this Presidency is going. Whether or not you like, or even love what Trump is…
key_points: The same biblical principles apply to any president: Jesus is on the throne and it is God who establishes authorities.
Romans 13 describes government as God's servant, and Christians should pray for leaders rather than put their trust in nations.
Psalm 46 means Christians have no reason to fear, whatever the political news.
Avoid nationalistic pride, and, like Daniel, stand for the truth of Scripture and accept the consequences.
This holds whether you like, hate or fear the president.

episodes.meta: Many of us think of the church as a building, but what is the Christian Church? In this episode we are going to explore that question, and how we as…
key_points: The church is not a building. The Bible speaks of the universal church, all believers of all times and places, and of local churches.
Jesus is the head of the church, which is his body.
Local churches keep believers connected, encourage them, and provide authority and the Lord's Supper.
The church serves one another and the world, meeting physical and spiritual needs.
The church carries out the Great Commission, so find a local church and use your spiritual gift there.
